- Overweight recent sentiment spikes in the 18-day history when forecasting short-term (next 30d) price movements — especially if sentiment > 0.7, model tends to overreact and overshoot.
- Underweight sentiment when price is trending downward — model often fails to correct downward momentum, leading to persistent overestimation of downside risk.
- When sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate price decline — apply a downward bias correction of 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects downward, leading to “overshoot then lag” pattern.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 1.5% above recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: for 30d forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, model tends to overestimate upside — cap forecast at +1.0% above 18-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model often misinterprets momentum — use sentiment smoothing (avg last 3 sentiment values) to reduce noise.
